title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

units.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
units.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.
units.idiomatic: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

units.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
units.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.
units.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

units.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
units.literal: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'
units.idiomatic: Once he was playing in the palace hall with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

units.zh: 惠帝乃止。
units.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

units.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
units.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.
units.idiomatic: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

units.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
units.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.
units.idiomatic: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

units.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
units.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'
units.idiomatic: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

units.zh: 由是奇之。
units.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.
units.idiomatic: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.

units.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
units.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'
units.idiomatic: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"

units.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
units.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.
units.idiomatic: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

units.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
units.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
units.idiomatic: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

units.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
units.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
units.idiomatic: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

units.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
units.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
units.idiomatic: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

units.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
units.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.
units.idiomatic: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.

units.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
units.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.
units.idiomatic: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.

units.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
units.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
units.idiomatic: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

units.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
units.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.
units.idiomatic: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.

units.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
units.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

units.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
units.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.
units.idiomatic: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

units.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
units.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.
units.idiomatic: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.

units.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
units.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.
units.idiomatic: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.

units.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
units.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.
units.idiomatic: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.

title.en: Volume 41: Book of Shu 11: Biographies of Huo, Wang, Xiang, Zhang, Yang, and Fei
title.raw: 卷四十一 蜀書十一 霍王向張楊費傳 Volume 41: Book of Shu 11: Biographies of Huo, Wang, Xiang, Zhang, Yang, and Fei

units.zh: 充闻之曰：“吾闻谯周之言，先帝讳备，其训具也，后主讳禅，其训授也，如言刘已具矣，当授与人也。
units.literal: Chong heard of it and said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's words: the Former Lord's taboo name Bei, its gloss is 'complete'; the Later Lord's taboo name Shan, its gloss is 'hand over'; as if saying the Liu house is already complete and should be handed to another.
units.idiomatic: Xiang Chong said: "I have heard Qiao Zhou's remark—the Former Lord's taboo name Bei means 'complete,' and the Later Lord's taboo name Shan means 'hand over,' as though the Liu house were finished and due to be handed on.

units.zh: 今中抚军名炎，而汉年极於炎兴，瑞出成都，而藏之於相国府，此殆天意也。”
units.literal: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, and the Han years end in Yanxing; the omen appeared at Chengdu yet is stored in the chancellor's mansion—this is perhaps heaven's intent.
units.idiomatic: Now the Central Pacifier is named Yan, Han's years end in Yanxing, the omen appeared at Chengdu and was stored in the chancellor's mansion—surely this is heaven's intent."

units.zh: 是岁，拜充为梓潼太守，明年十二月而晋武帝即尊位，炎兴於是乎徵焉。
units.literal: That year Chong was appointed Administrator of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin assumed the exalted position, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.
units.idiomatic: That year Xiang Chong was appointed governor of Zitong; in the twelfth month of the next year Emperor Wu of Jin took the throne, and Yanxing was thereby fulfilled.

units.zh: 孙盛曰：昔公孙自以起成都，号曰成氏，二玉之文，殆述所作乎！
units.literal: Sun Sheng said: Formerly Gongsun [Sun] took Chengdu as his rise and styled himself the Cheng clan—the text on the two jades perhaps describes what he wrought!
units.idiomatic: Sun Sheng said: When Gongsun Shu rose from Chengdu and styled himself the Cheng clan, the inscription on the two jades perhaps described what he had done!

units.zh: 此近赤祥也。
units.literal: This approximates a red portent.
units.idiomatic: These were red omens of the same kind.

units.zh: 晉武帝太康七年十一月，河陰有赤雪二頃。
units.literal: In the eleventh month of the seventh year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, at Heyin there was red snow covering two qing.
units.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the seventh Taikang year red snow covered two qing at Heyin.

units.zh: 此赤祥也。
units.literal: This is a red portent.
units.idiomatic: This was a red omen.

title.zh: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝
title.raw: 卷三 帝紀第三 世祖武帝 Volume 3 Annals 3: Emperor Wu

units.zh: 尊太妃王氏曰皇太后，宮曰崇化。
units.literal: He honored grand consort Wang as empress dowager, her residence titled Chonghua.
units.idiomatic: Lady Wang, the grand consort, became empress dowager with her palace named Chonghua.

units.zh: 封皇叔祖父孚爲安平王，皇叔父幹爲平原王，亮爲扶風王，伷爲東莞王，駿爲汝陰王，肜爲梁王，倫爲琅邪王，皇弟攸爲齊王，鑒爲樂安王，機爲燕王，[1]皇從伯父望爲義陽王，皇從叔父輔爲渤海王，晃爲下邳王，瑰爲太原王，珪爲高陽王，衡爲常山王，子文爲沛王，[2]泰爲隴西王，權爲彭城王，綏爲范陽王，遂爲濟南王，遜爲譙王，睦爲中山王，陵爲北海王，斌爲陳王，皇從父兄洪爲河間王，皇從父弟楙爲東平王。
units.literal: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping, his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ru'yin, Tong as king of Liang, Lun as king of Langye, his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Le'an, Ji as king of Yan, [1] his cousin once removed Wang as king of Yiyang, his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen, his cousin Hong as king of Hejian, and his cousin Mao as king of Dongping.
units.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping; his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ruyin, Tong as king of Liang, and Lun as king of Langye; his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Lean, and Ji as king of Yan; [1] his father's elder cousin Wang as king of Yiyang; his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen; his elder cousin Hong as king of Hejian; and his younger cousin Mao as king of Dongping.

units.zh: 以驃騎將軍石苞爲大司馬，封樂陵公，車騎將軍陳騫爲高平公，衛將軍賈充爲車騎將軍、魯公，尚書令裴秀爲鉅鹿公，侍中荀勖爲濟北公，太保鄭沖爲太傅、壽光公，太尉王祥爲太保、睢陵公，丞相何曾爲太尉、朗陵公，御史大夫王沈爲驃騎將軍、博陵公，司空荀顗爲臨淮公，鎮北大將軍衛瓘爲菑陽公。
units.literal: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, as grand marshal with enfeoffment as duke of Leling; Chen Qian, general of chariots and cavalry, as duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong, guard general, as general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu, supervisor of the masters of writing, as duke of Julu; Xun Xu, palace attendant, as duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong, grand guardian, as grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang, grand commandant, as grand protector and duke of Suiling; He Zeng, chancellor, as grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen, imperial counselor, as general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi, minister of works, as duke of Linhuai; Wei Guan, great general who guards the north, as duke of Ziyang.
units.idiomatic: He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, grand marshal and duke of Leling; Chen Qian duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu duke of Julu; Xun Xu duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang grand guardian and duke of Suiling; He Zeng grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi duke of Linhuai; and Wei Guan duke of Ziyang.

units.zh: 置中軍將軍，以統宿衛七軍。
units.literal: He established the general of the central army to command the seven palace-guard armies.
units.idiomatic: He created the post of general of the central army over seven inner garrisons.

units.zh: 己巳，詔陳留王載天子旌旗，備五時副車，行魏正朔，郊祀天地，禮樂制度皆如魏舊，上書不稱臣。
units.literal: On jisi he decreed that the king of Chenliu might use the Son of Heaven’s banners, maintain the five seasonal spare chariots, follow Wei’s calendar, sacrifice to heaven and earth, and keep music and ritual as under Wei, while memorials to him need not style the writer a subject.
units.idiomatic: On jisi the Chenliu king was allowed imperial pennons, five seasonal chariots, Wei’s calendar, full suburban rites, and Wei-style court music, with the privilege that petitioners omit the phrase “your subject.”

units.zh: 賜山陽公劉康、安樂公劉禪子弟一人爲駙馬都尉。
units.literal: He granted one descendant each of the mountain-yang duke Liu Kang and the duke of peace and ease Liu Shan the post of commandant of the consorts’ escort.
units.idiomatic: One son or younger kinsman each of Liu Kang, Duke of Shanyang, and Liu Shan, Duke of Anle, was granted the post of Commandant of the Consorts’ Escort.

units.zh: 二年春正月丙戌，遣兼侍中侯史光等持節四方，循省風俗，除禳祝之不在祀典者。
units.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on bingxu he sent concurrent palace attendant Hou Shiguang and others, bearing staffs of authority, to the four directions to tour and inspect customs, and to remove prayers and blessings not listed in the canonical sacrifices.
units.idiomatic: In the second year of Taishi, in spring, in the first month, on bingxu, Hou Shiguang and colleagues toured the empire with imperial staffs, removing exorcistic and prayer rites that were not in the ritual canon.

units.zh: 丁亥，有司請建七廟，帝重其役，不許。
units.literal: On dinghai the offices requested to build seven ancestral temples; the emperor, weighing the labor, did not grant it.
units.idiomatic: The ministry asked for seven-temple grandeur; the emperor refused, mindful of the burden.

units.zh: 庚寅，罷雞鳴歌。
units.literal: On gengyin he abolished the “cock-crow” song.
units.idiomatic: On gengyin he ended the dawn “cock-crow” anthem at court.

units.zh: 三月戊戌，吳人來弔祭，有司奏爲答詔。
units.literal: On wuxu of the third month Wu envoys came to offer condolences and sacrifices; the offices memorialized to prepare a reply edict.
units.idiomatic: Third month, wuxu: Wu’s envoys arrived for the funeral rites, and the clerks drafted a formal answer.

units.zh: 帝曰：「昔漢文、光武懷撫尉他、公孫述，皆未正君臣之儀，所以羈縻未賓也。
units.literal: The emperor said, "Of old Han Wen and Guangwu cherished and soothed Zhao Tuo and Gongsun Shu, and never regularized the rites of ruler and subject, thereby to bind those not yet submitted.
units.idiomatic: The emperor said: “Han Wen and Guangwu treated Zhao Tuo and Gongsun Shu generously without forcing full vassal etiquette—that was how they kept half-independent lords in play.

units.zh: 皓遣使之始，未知國慶，但以書答之。」
units.literal: When Hao first sent envoys he did not yet know of our state mourning; I answered only with a letter."
units.idiomatic: Sun Hao’s first embassy arrived before he knew we were in mourning; a simple letter sufficed.”

units.zh: 八月丙辰，省右將軍官。
units.literal: In the eighth month, on the day bingchen, the post of general of the right was abolished.
units.idiomatic: Eighth month, bingchen: the office of general of the right was struck from the rolls.

units.zh: 初，帝雖從漢魏之制，既葬除服，而深衣素冠，降席撤膳，哀敬如喪者。
units.literal: At first, although the emperor followed Han and Wei regulations and doffed mourning after the burial, he wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich foods from his table, grieving with the reverence of one still in mourning.
units.idiomatic: Though he had formally left mourning under Han–Wei precedent, he continued to dress plainly, eat simply, and keep the demeanor of a bereaved son.

units.zh: 戊辰，有司奏改服進膳，不許，遂禮終而後復吉。
units.literal: On the day wuchen the offices memorialized that he change to normal dress and resume a full diet; he did not grant it, and only when the mourning rites were complete did he return to auspicious observance.
units.idiomatic: Officials begged him on wuchen to set aside austerity; he refused until the last ritual day had passed.

title.zh: 卷九十 列傳第六十 良吏
title.raw: 卷九十 列傳第六十 良吏 Volume 90 Biographies 60: Good Officials

units.zh: 有晉肇茲王業，光啟霸圖，授方任能，經文緯武。
units.literal: When Jin founded its royal enterprise here and opened wide its hegemonic design, it assigned regions and employed worthies, ordering the civil realm and arraying the martial.
units.idiomatic: The Jin house raised its kingship and unfurled ambition across the realm, putting the right men in the right posts and pairing civil order with military strength.

units.zh: 泰始受禪，改物君臨，纂三葉之鴻基，膺百王之大寶，勞心庶績，垂意黎元，申敕守宰之司，婁發憂矜之詔，辭旨懇切，誨諭殷勤，欲使直道正身，抑末敦本。
units.literal: At Taishi, receiving the abdication and changing the mandate to rule as sovereign, inheriting the vast foundation of three reigns and receiving the great treasure passed down through a hundred kings, laboring over the myriad tasks of government and turning attention to the common people, repeatedly charging those who guarded and governed districts and issuing again and again edicts of anxious sympathy—wording earnest and urgent, instruction diligent—wishing to make officials walk the straight path and correct themselves, restraining the secondary and strengthening the root.
units.idiomatic: From the Taishi accession onward the throne changed hands peacefully; the dynasty inherited three generations of accumulated power and the nominal legitimacy of a long line of kings, toiled at every branch of administration, looked after the commoners, lectured prefects and magistrates again and again, and issued repeated edicts of heartfelt concern—demanding integrity, discipline, and a return to fundamental virtues.

units.zh: 當此時也，可謂農安其業，吏盡其能者歟！
units.literal: In such an hour, could one not say that farmers were secure in their occupations and clerks fulfilled their duties?
units.idiomatic: At that moment it seemed farmers could stay at their plows and officials actually did their jobs.

units.zh: 而帝寬厚足以君人，明威未能厲俗，政刑以之私謁，賄賂於此公行，結綬者以放濁為通，彈冠者以苟得為貴，流遁忘反，浸以為常。
units.literal: Yet the emperor's generous tolerance sufficed to rule men as lord, but his awesome clarity could not steel custom; government and punishments were bent by private soliciting, bribes ran openly here; those who tied their seals took looseness and corruption as 'getting through,' those who brushed caps took grasping gain as honor; drift and escape became forgetfulness of return, gradually entrenched as normal.
units.idiomatic: But imperial lenience let him govern without inspiring awe; customs did not stiffen. Justice bent to pull and patronage; gifts passed hands in broad daylight. Men who wore official cords treated laxity and graft as sophistication; men who entered office prized whatever they could grab. People slid away and forgot to return until vice passed for routine.

units.zh: 劉毅抗賣官之言，當時以為矯枉，察其風俗，豈虛也哉！
units.literal: Liu Yi spoke out against selling offices—people of the time thought him excessive in correcting a fault; observe the customs—was it empty talk?
units.idiomatic: When Liu Yi denounced the sale of offices, contemporaries called his remedy overwrought—yet look at how morals actually behaved, and his warning rings true.

units.zh: 五等建，封陰平伯。
units.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yinping.
units.idiomatic: Under the new five-rank nobility he became baron of Yinping.

units.zh: 武帝踐阼，轉鎮東將軍，進爵為侯。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, [Zhi] was transferred to General Who Guards the East and his noble rank was advanced to marquis.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne Zhi became General Who Guards the East and full marquis.

units.zh: 帝以芝清忠履正，素無居宅，使軍兵為作屋五十間。
units.literal: Because Zhi was pure, loyal, and upright in conduct and had never owned a dwelling, the emperor had soldiers build fifty rooms for him.
units.idiomatic: Seeing that Zhi was pure, loyal, and upright in conduct and had never owned a house, the emperor ordered fifty rooms built for him.

units.zh: 芝以年及懸車，告老遜位，章表十餘上，於是徵為光祿大夫，位特進，給吏卒，門施行馬。
units.literal: Zhi, feeling his years had reached the age to hang up his carriage [retire], requested retirement and yielded his position; memorials ran to more than ten submissions—whereupon he was summoned as Minister of the Imperial Household with nominal salary only, rank specially advanced, given clerks and soldiers, and a barrier gate was erected at his door.
units.idiomatic: Feeling he had reached retiring age, he repeatedly memorialized to step down—more than ten times—until the court recalled him as minister of the imperial household at nominal salary with specially advanced rank, staff and guards, and the privilege of a barrier gate.

units.zh: 羊祜為車騎將軍，乃以位讓芝，曰：「光祿大夫魯芝潔身寡欲，和而不同，服事華髮，以禮終始，未蒙此選，臣更越之，何以塞天下之望！」
units.literal: Yang Hu was General of Chariots and Cavalry and wished to yield his position to Zhi, saying: 'Minister of the Imperial Household Lu Zhi keeps himself pure with few desires, harmonizes without agreeing blindly, has served until his hair is hoary and observes ritual from first to last—he has not yet received this selection; if I leap past him, how shall I answer the hopes of the realm?'
units.idiomatic: Yang Hu was General of Chariots and Cavalry and wished to yield his position to Zhi, saying: 'Minister of the Imperial Household Lu Zhi keeps himself pure with few desires, harmonizes without agreeing blindly, has served until his hair is hoary and observes ritual from first to last—he has not yet received this selection; if I leap past him, how shall I answer the hopes of the realm?'

units.zh: 上不從。
units.literal: The emperor did not consent.
units.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

units.zh: 其為人所重如是。
units.literal: Such was the esteem in which others held him.
units.idiomatic: That was how highly peers valued him.

units.zh: 泰始九年卒，年八十四。
units.literal: In the ninth year of Taishi, he died at age eighty-four.
units.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taishi, he died at eighty-four.

units.zh: 帝為舉哀，賵贈有加，諡曰貞，賜塋田百畝。
units.literal: The emperor held mourning for him; burial gifts were augmented beyond the norm; his posthumous name was Zhen [Steadfast], and he was granted a burial plot of one hundred mu.
units.idiomatic: The emperor held mourning for him, burial gifts were given beyond the norm, his posthumous name was Zhen ('steadfast'), and he was granted a burial plot of one hundred mu.

units.zh: 胡威
units.literal: Hu Wei
units.idiomatic: Hu Wei

title.zh: 卷六十三 列傳第五十三 王神念 羊侃 羊鴉仁
title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第五十三 王神念 羊侃 羊鴉仁 Volume 63 Biographies 53: Wang Shennian, Yang Kan, Yang Ren

units.zh: 時少府奏新造兩刃矟成，長二丈四尺，圍一尺三寸。
units.literal: At that time the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues reported that a newly made double-edged spear was complete — length two zhang four chi, girth one chi three cun.
units.idiomatic: The Chamberlain of Palace Revenues announced that a new double-edged spear had been completed: twenty-four feet long with a shaft a foot and three inches around.

units.zh: 帝因賜侃河南國紫騮令試之。
units.literal: The emperor thereupon bestowed on Kan a purple stallion from Henan Commandery and ordered him to test it.
units.idiomatic: The emperor gave Kan a famed purple horse from Henan and told him to put the weapon through its paces.

units.zh: 侃執矟上馬，左右擊刺，特盡其妙。
units.literal: Kan took the spear, mounted, and thrust and stabbed to left and right, displaying its artistry to the utmost.
units.idiomatic: Kan mounted with the spear in hand and struck right and left with perfect mastery of the weapon.

units.zh: 觀者登樹。
units.literal: Those watching climbed trees.
units.idiomatic: Spectators scrambled up into the trees for a better view.

units.zh: 帝曰：「此樹必為侍中折矣。」
units.literal: The emperor said: "This tree will surely be broken by the Attendant-in-Ordinary."
units.idiomatic: The emperor remarked, "That tree won't survive the Attendant-in-Ordinary's display."

units.zh: 俄而果折，因號此矟為折樹矟。
units.literal: Before long it indeed broke, and so this spear was named the Tree-Breaking Spear.
units.idiomatic: Sure enough, the tree soon snapped, and from then on the spear was called the Tree-Breaker.

units.zh: 北人降者，唯侃是衣冠餘緒，帝寵之踰於他者，謂曰：「朕少時捉矟，形勢似卿，今失其舊體，殊覺不奇。」
units.literal: Among northerners who had surrendered, only Kan was descended from the robe-and-cap elite; the emperor favored him beyond the others and said: "In my youth when I wielded the spear my form resembled yours; now having lost my former build, I find it quite lacking in wonder."
units.idiomatic: Of all the northern defectors, only Kan came from the old gentry in cap and gown. The emperor favored him above the rest and said, "When I was young my spear-play looked much like yours. These days I've lost that old form, and by comparison nothing seems quite so marvelous."

units.zh: 上又制武宴詩三十韻示侃，侃即席上應詔。
units.literal: The emperor also composed a thirty-rhyme Martial Banquet Poem and showed it to Kan; Kan immediately at the feast responded to the imperial command.
units.idiomatic: The emperor then composed a thirty-couplet poem for the martial banquet and presented it to Kan, who answered on the spot from his seat.

units.zh: 帝覽曰：「吾聞仁者有勇，今見勇者有仁，可謂鄒、魯遺風，英賢不絕。」
units.literal: The emperor on reading said: "I have heard that the benevolent have courage; now I see one courageous who also has benevolence — truly the lingering wind of Zou and Lu, noble worthies never exhausted."
units.idiomatic: After reading it the emperor said, "They say the humane are brave; today I see bravery joined with humanity — the spirit of the sages of Zou and Lu still lives, and worthy men are not extinct."

units.zh: 是日詔入直殿省，啟尚方仗不堪用。
units.literal: That day he was ordered to enter and stand duty in the Palace Secretariat; he reported that the arsenal weapons were unfit for use.
units.idiomatic: That same day he was ordered into attendance at the Palace Secretariat, where he reported that the weapons in the imperial armory were shoddy and unusable.

units.zh: 務獻七寶床、象牙席。
units.literal: Wu presented a bed of seven treasures and an ivory mat.
units.idiomatic: Wu presented a seven-treasure bed and ivory mat.

units.zh: 詔曰：「昔晉武帝焚雉頭裘，朕常嘉之。
units.literal: The edict said: "Formerly Jin Emperor Wu burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always praised that.
units.idiomatic: The edict said, "Jin Emperor Wu burned the pheasant-head robe; I have always praised that.

units.zh: 今務所獻，亦此之流也。
units.literal: What Wu now presents is also of that sort.
units.idiomatic: What Wu presents is of that sort.

title.zh: 卷二十 志第十 禮中
title.raw: 卷二十 志第十 禮中 Volume 20 Treatises 10: Rites Part Two

units.zh: 群臣又固請，帝流涕久之乃許。
units.literal: The many ministers again firmly requested; the emperor wept a long time and then consented.
units.idiomatic: Ministers pressed until he wept long and yielded.

units.zh: 文明皇后崩及武元楊后崩，天下將吏發哀三日止。
units.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died and when Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died, officers throughout the realm raised mourning for three days and then stopped.
units.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Yuan died and when Empress Yang the consort of Wu died, officers empire-wide wailed three days only.

units.zh: 穆帝崩，哀帝立。
units.literal: When Emperor Mu died, Emperor Ai was enthroned.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Ai succeeded when Emperor Mu passed.

units.zh: 魏武以正月崩，魏文以其年七月設妓樂百戲，是則魏不以喪廢樂也。
units.literal: Wei Wu died in the first month; Wei Wen in that year's seventh month set singing-girls and the hundred entertainments—therefore Wei did not cancel music because of mourning.
units.idiomatic: Cao Cao died in the first month; Cao Pi still staged troupes and acrobats that seventh month—so Wei never treated mourning as a reason to silence the bands.

units.zh: 武帝以來，國有大喪，輒廢樂終三年。
units.literal: From Emperor Wu onward, whenever the state had great mourning, court music was suspended for the full three years.
units.idiomatic: Under Emperor Sima Yan, every dynastic bereavement silenced the orchestras for three years.

units.zh: 惠帝太安元年，太子喪未除，及元會亦廢樂。
units.literal: In the first year of Taian under Emperor Hui, the crown prince's mourning was not yet removed—yet for the New Year court assembly music was likewise suspended.
units.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui's Taian era, while the heir still wore mourning, the Yuan-day levee went without music.

units.zh: 高帝崩，遺詔加侍中。
units.literal: When Emperor Gao died, his final edict added the office of Attendant-in-Ordinary to Anren.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao died, his final edict added the office of Attendant-in-Ordinary to Anren.

units.zh: 武帝即位，為丹陽尹，遷尚書左僕射。
units.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anren became Intendant of Danyang and was transferred to Left Director of the Masters of Writing.
units.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anren became Intendant of Danyang and was transferred to Left Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 安人時屢啟密謀見賞，又善結尚書令王儉，故世傳儉啟有此授。
units.literal: At the time Anren was repeatedly rewarded for submitting secret plans and was also good at forming ties with Wang Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing, so people said that Jian had recommended this appointment.
units.idiomatic: At the time Anren was repeatedly rewarded for submitting secret plans and was also good at forming ties with Wang Jian, Director of the Masters of Writing, so people said that Jian had recommended this appointment.

title.zh: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下
title.raw: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下 Volume 23 Treatises 13: Music Part Two

units.zh: 大孝蒸蒸，德教被萬方。
units.literal: Great filial devotion steams upward--virtuous teaching covers myriad directions.
units.idiomatic: Filial steam rose thick; moral rain soaked every quarter.

units.zh: 于穆我皇
units.literal: Oh Solemn Our Sovereign
units.idiomatic: Oh Solemn Our Sovereign

units.zh: 于穆我皇，盛德聖且明。
units.literal: Oh solemn our emperor--flourishing virtue, sage and bright.
units.idiomatic: How solemn our sovereign, sage virtue blazing bright.

units.zh: 受禪君世，光濟群生。
units.literal: Receiving abdication he rules the age; glory aids the throng of lives.
units.idiomatic: He took abdication to shepherd the age and succor every life.

units.zh: 普天率土，莫不來庭。
units.literal: Throughout heaven's span and earth's soil--none fail to come to court.
units.idiomatic: Under heaven and across the soil every realm presents itself at court.

units.zh: 饗燕樂，受茲百祿，壽萬年。
units.literal: Feasting and banquet music--receiving these hundred blessings--life ten thousand years.
units.idiomatic: Feasts and music pour forth hundredfold blessings and span endless years.

units.zh: 唐堯諮務成，謙謙德其興。
units.literal: Tang Yao consulted Wucheng--modest modest--virtue thereby rises.
units.idiomatic: Yao of Tang asked counsel of Wucheng; humble humility lets virtue climb.

units.zh: 積漸終光大，履霜致堅冰。
units.literal: Accumulating gradual advance ends in great brightness--treading frost brings solid ice.
units.idiomatic: Grain on grain grows glory; tread frost and ice follows.

units.zh: 舜禹統百揆，元凱以次升。
units.literal: Shun and Yu commanded all offices--Yuan and Kai ascended in turn.
units.idiomatic: Shun and Yu ruled every bureau; Yuan and Kai rose in sequence.

units.zh: 禪讓應大曆，睿聖世相承。
units.literal: Abdition answered great calendar--wise and sacred ages handing on.
units.idiomatic: Abditions matched heaven's chronology; sage passed sage.

units.zh: 我皇陟帝位，平衡正準繩。
units.literal: Our emperor mounts emperor's throne--balance levels, guideline straight.
units.idiomatic: Our sovereign mounts the throne; scales hang level and lines stay true.

units.zh: 德化飛四表，祥氣見其徵。
units.literal: Virtuous transformation flies four outer regions--auspicious vapors show their signs.
units.idiomatic: Virtue flies to the four bounds; lucky mist proves every claim.

title.en: Volume 10: Book of Wei 10: Biographies of Xun Yu, Xun You, and Jia Xu
title.raw: 卷十 魏書十 荀彧荀攸賈詡傳 Volume 10: Book of Wei 10: Biographies of Xun Yu, Xun You, and Jia Xu

units.zh: 文帝即位，以詡爲太尉，《魏略》曰：文帝得詡之對太祖，故即位首登上司。
units.literal: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he made Xu Grand Commandant. The Brief Account of Wei states: Emperor Wen had obtained Xu's reply to the Grand Progenitor, and therefore upon taking the throne first appointed him to the supreme office.
units.idiomatic: When Cao Pi took the throne, he named Jia Xu Grand Commandant. The Brief Account of Wei explains that he remembered Jia Xu's counsel to Cao Cao and therefore promoted him first to the highest ministry.

units.zh: 荀勗別傳曰：晉司徒闕，武帝問其人於勗。
units.literal: The separate biography of Xun Xu states: The Jin office of Minister over the Masses was vacant; Emperor Wu asked Xu about the man for it.
units.idiomatic: A supplementary biography of Xun Xu records that when the Jin Minister over the Masses post fell vacant, Emperor Wu asked Xun Xu whom to appoint.

units.zh: 荅曰：「三公具瞻所歸，不可用非其人。
units.literal: He answered: "The three dukes are what all gaze upon and where they turn; one cannot use someone who is not the right man.
units.idiomatic: He answered, "The Three Excellencies are what the whole court looks to; you cannot fill such a post with the wrong man.

title.zh: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上
title.en: Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One
title.raw: 卷三十一 列傳第一 后妃上 Volume 31 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts Part One

units.zh: 父駿，別有傳。
units.literal: Her father Jun has a separate biography.
units.idiomatic: Her father Yang Jun has his own biography.

units.zh: 以咸寧二年立為皇后。
units.literal: In the second Xianning year she was established as empress.
units.idiomatic: She became empress in 276.

units.zh: 婉嫕有婦德，美映椒房，甚有寵。
units.literal: Gracious and yielding, she possessed womanly virtue; her beauty lit the pepper chambers and she enjoyed deep favor.
units.idiomatic: Gentle and virtuous, she brightened the harem and won enduring favor.

units.zh: 生渤海殤王，早薨，遂無子。
units.literal: She bore Prince Huaihai of Bohai, who died young; thereafter she had no sons.
units.idiomatic: Her son the prince of Bohai died in infancy, leaving her without heirs.

units.zh: 太康九年，后率內外夫人命婦躬桑于西郊，賜帛各有差。
units.literal: In the ninth Taikang year the empress led palace ladies and titled wives to tend silkworms at the western suburb and granted silk in graded amounts.
units.idiomatic: In 288 she led court ladies to the western suburban silkworm rite and dispensed silk rewards by rank.

units.zh: 太子妃賈氏妒忌，帝將廢之。
units.literal: Crown Princess Jia was jealous; the emperor was about to depose her.
units.idiomatic: Jealous Crown Princess Jia faced deposition.

units.zh: 后言於帝曰：「賈公閭有勳社稷，猶當數世宥之。
units.literal: The empress said to the emperor: “Lord Jia has merit for state—his house deserves indulgence for generations.
units.idiomatic: She urged him, “Jia Chong secured the dynasty—his clan merits lasting grace.

units.zh: 賈妃親是其女，正復妒忌之間，不足以一眚掩其大德。」
units.literal: The Jia consort is his own daughter; amid jealousy alone, one blemish cannot veil his great virtue.”
units.idiomatic: His daughter is princess—in mere spite one flaw cannot bury his great merit."

units.zh: 后又數誡厲妃，妃不知后之助己，因以致恨，謂后構之於帝，忿怨彌深。
units.literal: Later she repeatedly warned and rebuked the princess; the princess did not realize the empress aided her and therefore bore hatred, believing the empress framed her before the emperor—resentment grew deeper.
units.idiomatic: She later scolded the princess repeatedly; blind to this help, Jia Nanfeng blamed her for slander and hated her all the more.

units.zh: 及帝崩，尊為皇太后。
units.literal: When the emperor died, she was honored as empress dowager.
units.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu died she became empress dowager.

units.zh: 賈后凶悖，忌后父駿執權，遂誣駿為亂，使楚王瑋與東安王繇稱詔誅駿。
units.literal: Empress Jia was vicious; she resented her father Jun holding power, then slandered Jun as rebellious and had Prince Chu Wei and Prince Dongan Yao forge edicts to execute Jun.
units.idiomatic: Vicious Jia Nanfeng feared Yang Jun; she accused him of treason and had Sima Wei and Sima Yao murder him with forged orders.

units.zh: 昔文姜與亂，春秋所貶，呂宗叛戾，高后降配，宜廢皇太后為峻陽庶人。」
units.literal: Formerly Wen Jiang joined turmoil—the Spring and Autumn demoted her; the Lü clan rebelled and Empress Gao was lowered in pairing. She should be demoted from empress dowager to commoner of Junyang.”
units.idiomatic: Like Wen Jiang or Empress Lü, she must be struck from dowager rank and made a commoner of Junyang.”

units.zh: 中書監張華等以為「太后非得罪于先帝者也，今黨惡所親，[3]為不母于聖世。
units.literal: Palace Supervisor Zhang Hua and others held: “The dowager did not offend the late emperor; now she joins wicked kin—she fails motherhood toward this sage age [3].
units.idiomatic: Zhang Hua argued: “She never wronged Emperor Wu; siding with villains now breaks maternal duty in our era [3].

units.zh: 宜依孝成趙皇后故事，曰武帝皇后，處之離宮，以全貴終之恩。」
units.literal: She should follow Empress Zhao of Emperor Cheng’s precedent—styled Empress of Emperor Wu and housed in a detached palace to preserve honored kindness to the end.”
units.idiomatic: Treat her like Chengdi’s Zhao—call her Emperor Wu’s consort, lodge her apart, yet grant a decent end.”

units.zh: 尚書令、下邳王晃等議曰：「皇太后與駿潛謀，欲危社稷，不可復奉承宗廟，配合先帝。
units.literal: The Director of the Department of State Affairs, Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi, and others debated: “The empress dowager secretly plotted with Jun to overturn the state—she cannot again serve the temple or pair with the late emperor.
units.idiomatic: Sima Huang, Prince of Xiapi and Director of the Department of State Affairs, countered: “She conspired with Yang Jun—she cannot share Wu’s temple.

units.zh: 宜貶尊號，廢詣金墉城。」
units.literal: Her honored title should be stripped and she banished to Metal-Walled Fortress.”
units.idiomatic: Strip her titles and lock her in Jinyong.”

units.zh: 初，太后尚有侍御十餘人，賈后奪之，絕膳而崩，時年三十四，在位十五年。
units.literal: At first the dowager still had more than ten attendants; Empress Jia seized them; she starved and died, aged thirty-four, having held rank fifteen years.
units.idiomatic: Jia stripped her servants; she starved at thirty-four after fifteen years as consort.

units.zh: 賈后又信妖巫，謂太后必訴冤先帝，乃覆而殯之，施諸厭劾符書藥物。
units.literal: Empress Jia further trusted witchcraft, fearing the dowager would appeal her grievance to the late emperor; she therefore buried her face-down with curse charms and drugs.
units.idiomatic: Jia feared her ghost would accuse Emperor Wu, so she buried her prone under talismans.

units.zh: 永嘉元年，追復尊號，別立廟，神主不配武帝。
units.literal: In the first year of Yongjia her honored title was restored, a separate temple was established, and her spirit tablet was not paired with Emperor Wu.
units.idiomatic: In 307 her title was restored, a separate shrine was built, and her tablet was not enshrined with Emperor Wu.

units.zh: 至成帝咸康七年，下詔使內外詳議。
units.literal: By the seventh year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng, an edict ordered inner and outer officials to debate the matter in detail.
units.idiomatic: In 341 Emperor Cheng ordered court and capital officials to deliberate the question fully.

units.zh: 衛將軍虞潭議曰：世祖武皇帝光有四海，元皇后應乾作配。
units.literal: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Shizu Emperor Wu glorified the four seas; his primal empress matched Heaven’s pivot.”
units.idiomatic: Guards General Yu Tan argued: “Emperor Wu illumined the realm; his first empress answered Heaven.”

units.zh: 元后既崩，悼后繼作，至楊駿肆逆，禍延天母。
units.literal: After the primal empress died, the mourned empress succeeded; when Yang Jun ran riot, calamity reached the Mother of Heaven.
units.idiomatic: After Yang Yan died came Yang Zhi; Yang Jun’s treason dragged down the queen mother.

units.zh: 蓋是事之未盡，非義典也。
units.literal: That was because the matter was unfinished—not canonical meaning.
units.idiomatic: That showed work unfinished, not proper liturgy.

units.zh: 若以悼后復位為宜，則應配食世祖；
units.literal: If restoring Empress Dao is right, she should share Emperor Wu’s offerings;
units.idiomatic: If Yang Zhi deserves restoration, she must join Wu’s temple;

units.zh: 若以復之為非，則譜諡宜闕，未有位號居正，而偏祠別室者也。
units.literal: if restoring her is wrong, then genealogies and epithets should lapse—one cannot hold orthodox rank yet dwell in a side shrine alone.
units.idiomatic: if not, her titles should lapse—no legitimate rank receives only a side altar.

units.zh: 若以孝懷皇帝私隆母子之道，特為立廟者，此苟崇私情，有虧國典，則國譜帝諱，皆宜除棄，匪徒不得同祀于世祖之廟也。
units.literal: If Emperor Huai privately enlarged mother-son feeling and built a special temple, that would exalt private affection yet wound state canon—then clan registers and temple names should all be discarded, not merely barred from Wu’s temple.
units.idiomatic: A private shrine for filial piety alone would break precedent and void every register.

units.zh: 會稽王昱、中書監庾冰、中書令何充、尚書令諸葛恢、尚書謝廣、光祿勳留擢、丹楊尹殷融、護軍將軍馮懷、散騎常侍鄧逸等咸從潭議，由是太后配食武帝。
units.literal: Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, Palace Supervisor Yu Bing, Palace Director He Chong, Minister Director Zhuge Hui, Minister Xie Guang, Superintendent of the Household Liu Zhuo, Intendant of Danyang Yin Rong, Defender-general Feng Huai, and Palace Rider Deng Yi all followed Tan’s opinion; thereby the dowager shared Emperor Wu’s sacrifices.
units.idiomatic: Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, Yu Bing, He Chong, Zhuge Hui, Xie Guang, Liu Zhuo, Yin Rong, Feng Huai, and Deng Yi endorsed Tan—Yang Zhi joined Wu’s temple.

units.zh: 左貴嬪
units.literal: Honorable Lady Zuo
units.idiomatic: Lady Zuo of Honorable Rank

units.zh: 兄思，別有傳。
units.literal: Her brother Si has a separate biography.
units.idiomatic: Her brother Zuo Si has his own biography.

units.zh: 芬少好學，善綴文，名亞于思，武帝聞而納之。
units.literal: Fen from youth loved learning, excelled at composing, her fame second only to Si’s; Emperor Wu heard of her and took her in.
units.idiomatic: A scholar and poet second only to Zuo Si, she entered Emperor Wu’s harem by reputation.

units.zh: 泰始八年，拜修儀。
units.literal: In the eighth Taishi year she was appointed Xiuyi.
units.idiomatic: In 272 she became Xiuyi.

title.raw: 卷四十八 楊李翟應霍爰徐列傳 Volume 48: Biographies of Yang, Li, Di, Ying, Huo, Yuan, Xu

units.zh: 詁音古。
units.literal: Gu is read like gu meaning 'explain.'
units.idiomatic: The commentary glosses gu with the usual reading for exegesis.

units.zh: 初，酺之為大匠，上言：「孝文皇帝始置一經博士，[一]武帝大合天下之書，[二] 而孝宣論六經於石渠，學者滋盛，弟子萬數。
units.literal: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.
units.idiomatic: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.

units.zh: [三]光武初興，愍其荒廢，起太學博士捨、內外講堂，諸生橫巷，為海內所集。
units.literal: [3] When Guangwu first rose, pitying their ruin and waste, he raised the Grand Academy, erudite lodgings, inner and outer lecture halls, and lanes of students—it became the gathering place of the realm.
units.idiomatic: [3] Emperor Guangwu, grieving the ruin of learning, had rebuilt the Grand Academy with dormitories, inner and outer lecture halls, and student quarters that drew scholars from everywhere.

units.zh: 酺免後，遂起太學，更開拓房室，學者為酺立碑銘於學雲。
units.literal: After Pu was dismissed, thereupon they raised the Grand Academy, again opened and expanded rooms, and scholars set up a stele inscription for Pu at the academy, it is said.
units.idiomatic: After his disgrace the Grand Academy was rebuilt and expanded; students are said to have raised a stele in his honor on the campus.

units.zh: 注[一]武帝建元五年始置五經博士，文帝之時未遑庠序之事，酺之此言，不知何據。
units.literal: Note [1] In Emperor Wu's Jianyuan 5 the five-classics erudites were first established; in Emperor Wen's time there was not yet leisure for school matters—what Pu's statement relies on is unknown.
units.idiomatic: Commentary [1]: Emperor Wu first established Erudites for the Five Classics in the fifth year of Jianyuan. In Emperor Wen's time there was not yet leisure for affairs of schools and academies, so it is unclear what authority Zhai Pu had for this statement.

units.zh: 注[二]武帝詔曰：「其令禮官勸學，舉遺興禮。」
units.literal: Note [2] Emperor Wu's edict said: 'Let the ritual officials encourage learning and raise the lost and promote ritual.'
units.idiomatic: Commentary [2]: "Emperor Wu had ordered the ritual bureau to revive neglected learning and rites."

units.zh: 舉遺謂搜求遺逸，是合天下之書也。
units.literal: Raise the lost' means to search out the scattered and hidden—this is gathering the books of All under Heaven.'
units.idiomatic: Raising the lost meant recovering lost texts, that is, the empire-wide book hunt.

title.zh: 卷二十 志第十 禮中
title.raw: 卷二十 志第十 禮中 Volume 20 Treatises 10: Rites Part Two

units.zh: 文多不載。
units.literal: The text is extensive and is not recorded here.
units.idiomatic: The compilation ran long and is omitted here.

units.zh: 武帝楊悼皇后既母養懷帝，后遇難時，懷帝尚幼，及即位，中詔述后恩愛。
units.literal: Empress Yang Dao of Emperor Wu had already mother-nurtured Emperor Huai; when she later met violent death, Emperor Huai was still young; when he ascended, an inner edict recounted the empress's kindness and love.
units.idiomatic: Empress Yang had raised the future Emperor Huai; when she was killed he was still a child, and on enthronement he issued a palace rescript praising her care.

units.zh: 及后祖載，群官議帝應為追制服，或以庶母慈己，依禮制小功五月，或以謂慈母服如母服齊衰者，眾議不同。
units.literal: When later her funeral train departed, the many offices debated whether the emperor ought wear retroactive mourning—or some said because a concubine-mother had loved him, by ritual he should wear xiao gong five months—or some said foster-mother mourning like a mother's qi-cui—the many opinions differed.
units.idiomatic: At her cortège the ministries split: some wanted retroactive weeds, some cited a nurturing concubine's xiao gong, some equated her to a legal mother in qi-cui.

units.zh: 閭丘沖議云：「楊后母養聖上，蓋以曲情。
units.literal: Luqiu Chong debated: 'Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally out of special affection.
units.idiomatic: Luqiu Chong debated: 'Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally out of special affection.

units.zh: 今以恩禮追崇，不配世祖廟。
units.literal: Now by kindness and ritual we posthumously honor her—not pairing her in Emperor Shizu's temple.
units.idiomatic: Now by kindness and ritual we posthumously honor her—not pairing her in Emperor Shizu's temple.

units.zh: 王者無慈養之服，謂宜祖載之日，可三朝素服發哀而已。」
units.literal: For kings there is no garment for 'foster nurturing'; I say on the day of the funeral train, three court sessions in plain dress to raise mourning is enough.'
units.idiomatic: For kings there is no garment for 'foster nurturing'; I say on the day of the funeral train, three court sessions in plain dress to raise mourning is enough.'

title.en: Volume 45 Biographies 15: Liu Yi; Cheng Wei; He Jiao; Wu Gai; Ren Kai; Cui Hong; Guo Yi; Hou Shiguang; He Pan
title.raw: 卷四十五 列傳第十五 劉毅 和嶠 武陔 任愷 崔洪 郭奕 侯史光 何攀 Volume 45 Biographies 15: Liu Yi; Cheng Wei; He Jiao; Wu Gai; Ren Kai; Cui Hong; Guo Yi; Hou Shiguang; He Pan

units.zh: 太傅從事中郎庾敳見而歎曰：「嶠森森如千丈松，雖磥砢有節目，施之大廈，有棟樑之用。」
units.literal: Adjutant to the grand tutor Yu Ai saw him and sighed: "Jiao stands tall like a thousand-foot pine—though gnarled and knotty—applied to a great hall—has timber-and-beam use."
units.idiomatic: Yu Ai marveled: "He Jiao is a thousand-foot pine—rough bark and all—yet palace timber."

units.zh: 賈充亦重之，稱于武帝，入為給事黃門侍郎，遷中書令，帝深器遇之。
units.literal: Jia Chong also esteemed him—praised him to Emperor Wu—entered as gentleman attendant at the yellow gate—promoted director of the palace secretariat—Emperor deeply prized him.
units.idiomatic: Jia Chong praised him to the throne; he entered the palace secretariat and became an imperial favorite.

units.zh: 舊監令共車入朝，時荀勖為監，嶠鄙勖為人，以意氣加之，每同乘，高抗專車而坐。
units.literal: By old practice overseer and director shared carriage into court—at time Xun Xu was overseer—Jiao despised Xu’s person—applied spirit of pride—each time riding together—held head high and sat exclusive carriage.
units.idiomatic: Overseer and director once rode together; Jiao scorned Xun Xu and insisted on a separate cart.

units.zh: 嶠轉侍中，愈被親禮，與任愷、張華相善。
units.literal: Jiao transferred to palace attendant—more favored—in friendship with Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.
units.idiomatic: As palace attendant he grew closer to the throne and befriended Ren Kai and Zhang Hua.

units.zh: 嶠見太子不令，因侍坐曰：「皇太子有淳古之風，而季世多偽，恐不了陛下家事。」
units.literal: Jiao seeing heir apparent was not sound—therefore sitting attendance said: "Crown prince has pure antique manner—but declining age abounds in sham—fears he cannot manage Your Majesty’s household affairs."
units.idiomatic: At leisure he said: "The crown prince has an antique plainness, yet a decadent age breeds sham—I fear he cannot manage Your Majesty's household."

units.zh: 帝默然不答。
units.literal: Emperor silent—did not answer.
units.idiomatic: The emperor stayed silent.

units.zh: 後與荀顗、荀勖同侍，帝曰：「太子近入朝，差長進，卿可俱詣之，粗及世事。」
units.literal: Later together attending with Xun Yi and Xun Xu—Emperor said: "Heir apparent lately entered court—somewhat grown—you may all visit him—roughly touch on worldly affairs."
units.idiomatic: Later, with the Xuns attending, the emperor said: "The heir has lately entered court and made some progress—you may all visit him and touch on affairs of state."

units.zh: 即奉詔而還。
units.literal: Immediately obeyed edict and returned.
units.idiomatic: They bowed and withdrew.

units.zh: 嶠曰：「聖質如初耳！」
units.literal: Jiao said: "Sagely substance like first!"
units.idiomatic: He Jiao said: "His sagely substance is just as before!"

units.zh: 帝不悅而起。
units.literal: Emperor displeased—rose.
units.idiomatic: The emperor rose in anger.

units.zh: 嶠退居，恆懷慨歎，知不見用，猶不能已。
units.literal: Jiao withdrew—always harbored sighing regret—knew not employed—still could not stop.
units.idiomatic: He brooded—knowing his counsel spurned yet unable to stay mute.

units.zh: 在御坐言及社稷，未嘗不以儲君為憂。
units.literal: On imperial seat speaking of altars of soil and grain—never without taking heir as worry.
units.idiomatic: Whenever talk touched the realm’s fate he fretted over the heir.

units.zh: 帝知其言忠，每不酬和。
units.literal: Emperor knew his words loyal—each time did not respond in harmony.
units.idiomatic: The emperor knew him faithful yet refused to engage.

units.zh: 後與嶠語，不及來事。
units.literal: Later speaking with Jiao—did not reach future matters.
units.idiomatic: Later audiences skirted the succession entirely.

units.zh: 賈后使帝問嶠曰：「卿昔謂我不了家事，今日定云何？」
units.literal: Empress Jia had Emperor ask Jiao: "You once said I could not manage household affairs—today settled how?"
units.idiomatic: The empress had the emperor ask him: "You once said I could not manage the household—what is your judgment today?"

units.zh: 嶠曰：「臣昔事先帝，曾有斯言。
units.literal: Jiao said: "Your servant formerly served late Emperor—once had this saying.
units.idiomatic: He Jiao said: "Your servant once served the late emperor and spoke this warning.

units.zh: 言之不效，國之福也。
units.literal: Words not fulfilled—state’s fortune.
units.idiomatic: That it proved false was the realm’s luck.

units.zh: =茂以德素稱，名亞於陔，為上洛太守、散騎常侍、侍中、尚書。
units.literal: =Mao by plain virtue praised—name second to Gai—prefect of Shangluo—regular attendant at casual riding—attendant-in-ordinary—minister of state affairs.
units.idiomatic: Wu Mao, famed for plain virtue just below Wu Gai, governed Shangluo and reached the ministries.

units.zh: 潁川荀愷年少於茂，即武帝姑子，自負貴戚，欲與茂交，距而不答，由是致怨。
units.literal: Yingchuan Xun Kai younger than Mao—being Emperor Wu’s cousin by aunt—self-important as noble kin—wished befriend Mao—refused distance—thereby incurred resentment.
units.idiomatic: Xun Kai of Yingchuan, younger than Mao and a son of Emperor Wu’s paternal aunt, prided himself on noble kinship, wished to befriend Mao, was refused, and therefore resented him.

units.zh: 及楊駿誅，愷時為僕射，以茂駿之姨弟，陷為逆黨，遂見害。
units.literal: When Yang Jun executed—Kai then vice director—because Mao Jun’s maternal nephew—trapped as rebel clique—thereupon harmed.
units.idiomatic: After Yang Jun fell, Xun Kai framed Wu Mao as Jun’s kin and had him killed.

units.zh: 並遺宛馬一匹，血從前髆上小孔中出。
units.literal: Together leave Wan horse one piece—blood from front shoulder blade upper small hole emerges.
units.idiomatic: With it goes a Ferghana horse whose blood beads from a pore on the shoulder.

units.zh: 常聞武帝歌天馬，沾赤汗，今親見其然也。
units.literal: Constantly heard Martial Emperor sing heaven horse—stained red sweat—now personally see it thus.
units.idiomatic: I grew up on the songs of Emperor Wu's sweating steeds—now I have seen one.

units.zh: 頃反虜尚屯，將帥在外，憂念遑遑，未有閒寧。
units.literal: [68] Recently rebel captives still camp—generals outside—worry thought restless—have not yet idle peace.
units.idiomatic: [68] Rebels still hold the field and our generals are abroad—I have no peace of mind.

title.zh: 卷51 列傳第16 長孫覽
title.raw: 卷51 列傳第16 長孫覽 Volume 51 Biographies 16: Zhang Sunlan

units.zh: 諡曰靜。
units.literal: His posthumous title was Jing.
units.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Jing ("Tranquil").

units.zh: 子安世，通事謁者。
units.literal: His son Anshi was a Master of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests.
units.idiomatic: His son Anshi served as Master of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests.

units.zh: 熾弟晟晟字季晟，性通敏，略涉書記，善彈工射，趫捷過人。
units.literal: Chi's younger brother Sheng—Sheng, courtesy name Jisheng, was penetrating and quick by nature, had a slight acquaintance with written records, was skilled at archery and mounted shooting, and was exceptionally agile.
units.idiomatic: Chi's younger brother Zhangsun Sheng—Sheng, whose courtesy name was Jisheng, was quick-witted and responsive, knew something of clerical work, excelled at archery and mounted shooting, and was unusually nimble.

units.zh: 時周室尚武，貴遊子弟鹹以相矜，每共馳射，時輩皆出其下。
units.literal: At that time the Zhou court valued martial prowess; the sons of the nobility all prided themselves on one another; whenever they rode and shot together, their contemporaries fell below him.
units.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou court then prized martial arts, and young men of noble families vied with one another; whenever they rode and shot together, none of his peers could match him.

title.zh: 卷四十七 列傳第十七 傅玄
title.raw: 卷四十七 列傳第十七 傅玄 Volume 47 Biographies 17: Fu Xuan

units.zh: 三旬之間，遷司徒左長史。
units.literal: Within thirty days he was promoted to senior clerk in the left of the minister of education.
units.idiomatic: Within thirty days he was promoted to senior clerk on the left of the minister of education.

units.zh: 時帝留心政事，詔訪朝臣政之損益。
units.literal: At that time the emperor applied his mind to government affairs; an edict inquired of court ministers about harm and benefit in administration.
units.idiomatic: The emperor was then intent on government and issued an edict asking the ministers what in current policy helped or harmed the realm.

units.zh: 咸上言曰：「陛下處至尊之位，而修布衣之事，親覽萬機，勞心日昃。
units.literal: Xian submitted words saying: "Your Majesty occupies the supremely honored position, yet cultivates common-cloth affairs, personally inspects ten thousand threads, and toils in mind until the sun slants.
units.idiomatic: Fu Xian submitted a memorial: "Although Your Majesty occupies the highest throne, you still take on a commoner's workload, personally attending to every matter of government, laboring in mind until the sun stands in the west.

units.zh: 在昔帝王，躬自菲薄，以利天下，未有逾陛下也。
units.literal: Among emperors and kings of the past who personally practiced meagerness to benefit all under Heaven, none has exceeded Your Majesty.
units.idiomatic: Among the emperors of old who wore austerity on their own backs for the good of the realm, none has outdone you.

units.zh: 然泰始開元以暨於今，十有五年矣。
units.literal: Yet from the opening of Taishi down to the present, there are already fifteen years.
units.idiomatic: Yet fifteen years have passed since the Taishi era began.

units.zh: 逮至漢文，以天下體大，服重難久，遂制既葬而除。
units.literal: Down to Emperor Wen of Han, because the realm under Heaven was large in scale and heavy mourning could not be prolonged long, thereupon the rule was to remove mourning garments once burial was complete.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han, seeing the realm too vast for prolonged heavy mourning, decreed that mourning dress end with the burial.

units.zh: 世祖武皇帝雖大孝蒸蒸，亦從時釋服，制心喪三年，至於萬機之事，則有不遑。
units.literal: Our founding emperor Emperor Wu, though his filial devotion was abundant, also followed the times in laying aside mourning garments, setting heart-mourning for three years; as for the ten thousand threads of business, then there was no leisure.
units.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, our dynastic founder, was deeply filial, yet he too laid aside formal mourning when the times required it, keeping a three-year grief in his heart while knowing he could not neglect the myriad tasks of rule.

units.zh: 今聖上欲委政於公，諒暗自居，此雖謙讓之心，而天下未以為善。
units.literal: Now the sagely sovereign wishes to entrust government to your lordship and dwell in mourning seclusion himself—this, although a mind of yielding, is not what all under Heaven takes for good.
units.idiomatic: The reigning emperor wishes to leave government in your hands while he withdraws in mourning; that may show modest intent, but the empire does not read it as wise.

title.zh: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下
title.raw: 卷二十三 志第十三 樂下 Volume 23 Treatises 13: Music Part Two

units.zh: 大晉承運期
units.literal: Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season
units.idiomatic: Great Jin Receives the Mandate's Season

units.zh: 大晉承運期，德隆聖皇。
units.literal: Great Jin receives the mandate's season--virtue lofty, sage emperor.
units.idiomatic: Great Jin took heaven's hour; virtue rose with the sage throne.

units.zh: 時清晏，白日垂光。
units.literal: Times pure and tranquil--bright sun hangs radiance.
units.idiomatic: The age grew clear and still; the bright sun hung steady.

units.zh: 應籙圖，陟帝位，繼天正玉衡。
units.literal: Answering tally charts--ascending emperor's throne--continuing heaven, correcting jade armillary.
units.idiomatic: Portents answered; he mounted the throne and aligned heaven's armillary.

units.zh: 化行象神明，至哉道隆虞與唐。
units.literal: Transforming conduct images spirit luminaries--ultimate indeed Way lofty as Yu and Tang.
units.idiomatic: Conduct mirrored the gods; his Way rivaled Yu and Tang.

units.zh: 元首敷洪化，百僚股肱並忠良。
units.literal: Head spreads vast transformation--hundred officials as thighs and arms, together loyal and good.
units.idiomatic: The sovereign spread vast change; every minister served as limb and loyal heart.

units.zh: 時太康，隆隆赫赫，福祚盈無疆。
units.literal: Times reach Grand Peace--towering and blazing--blessing throne overflows without bound.
units.idiomatic: Tai Kang dawned in towering blaze; blessing flooded without limit.

units.zh: 聖徵見，參日月。
units.literal: Sacred omens appear--joining sun and moon.
units.idiomatic: Sacred signs appeared beside sun and moon.

units.zh: 惟我皇，體神聖。
units.literal: Only our emperor--embodies spirit sagacity.
units.idiomatic: Our sovereign bodies forth spirit-wisdom.

units.zh: 受魏禪，應天命。
units.literal: Receiving Wei's abdication--answering heaven's mandate.
units.idiomatic: He took Wei's abdication and answered heaven.

units.zh: 皇之興，靈有徵。
units.literal: Emperor's rising--spirit has omens.
units.idiomatic: His ascent bore spirit omens.

units.zh: 得漢郡者十有八焉。
units.literal: Those obtaining Han commanderies were eighteen.
units.idiomatic: Wu in the end controlled eighteen commanderies that had once belonged to Han.

units.zh: 晉武帝太康元年，既平孫氏，凡增置郡國二十有三，
units.literal: Jin Emperor Wu, Taikang first year, having already pacified the Sun clan, in all added twenty-three commanderies and kingdoms,
units.idiomatic: In the first year of Taikang, after Jin Wudi crushed the Sun regime, the court created twenty-three new commanderies and kingdoms,

units.zh: 〈滎陽、上洛、頓丘、臨淮、東莞、襄城、汝陰、長廣、廣甯、昌黎、新野、隨郡、陰平、義陽、毗陵、宣城、南康、晉安、寧浦、始平、略陽、樂平、南平。〉
units.literal: 〈Yingyang, Shangluo, Dunqiu, Linhuai, Dongguan, Xiangcheng, Ru'yin, Changguang, Guangning, Changli, Xinye, Sui commandery, Yinping, Yiyang, Piling, Xuancheng, Nankang, Jin'an, Ningpu, Shiping, Lueyang, Leping, Nanping.〉

title.zh: 卷23 漢紀十五
title.raw: 卷23 漢紀十五

units.zh: 秋，大鴻臚廣明、軍正王平擊益州，斬首、捕虜三萬餘人，獲畜產五萬餘頭。
units.literal: In autumn, Grand Herald Guangming and Army Rectifier Wang Ping attacked Yizhou; heads cut off and captives taken exceeded thirty thousand, and livestock obtained exceeded fifty thousand head.
units.idiomatic: In autumn, Grand Herald Guangming and Army Rectifier Wang Ping attacked Yizhou, beheading and capturing more than thirty thousand men and taking more than fifty thousand head of livestock.

units.zh: 諫大夫杜延年見國家承武帝奢侈、師旅之後，數為大將軍光言：「年歲比不登，流民未盡還，宜修孝文時政，示以儉約、寬和，順天心，說民意，年歲宜應。」
units.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Du Yannian, seeing the state inherit Emperor Wu's extravagance and campaigns, repeatedly spoke to Grand General Guang: "Years in succession have not had good harvests; displaced people have not all returned—it is fitting to restore Emperor Wen's policies, show frugality and restraint and lenience and harmony, accord with Heaven's heart, please the people's intent, and the years ought to respond."
units.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Du Yannian, seeing the state inherit Emperor Wu's extravagance and campaigns, repeatedly told Grand General Guang, "Harvests have failed year after year and displaced people have not all returned. It is fitting to restore Emperor Wen's policies, show frugality, restraint, lenience, and harmony, accord with Heaven's heart, please the people, and the years ought to respond."

units.zh: 光納其言。
units.literal: Guang accepted his words.
units.idiomatic: Guang accepted his counsel.

units.zh: 安危不可知，子卿尚復誰為乎！」
units.literal: Safety and danger cannot be known—Ziqing, for whom do you still act!"
units.idiomatic: Safety and danger cannot be known—for whom do you still act, Ziqing!"

units.zh: 武曰：「武父子無功德，皆為陛下所成就，位列將，爵通侯，兄弟親近，常願肝腦塗地。
units.literal: Wu said: "Wu father and son had no merit or virtue—all were accomplished by Your Majesty; we ranked as generals, enfeoffed as full marquises, brothers close and near, and constantly wished to smear liver and brain on the ground.
units.idiomatic: Wu said, "Wu father and son had no merit—all was accomplished by Your Majesty. We ranked as generals, were enfeoffed as full marquises, and as close brothers constantly wished to lay down our lives.

units.zh: 今得殺身自效，雖斧鉞、湯鑊，誠甘樂之！
units.literal: Now obtaining to kill the body and devote effect, though axe and halberd, boiling cauldron, truly I would gladly enjoy it!
units.idiomatic: Now to be able to give my life in service, though it be axe and halberd or boiling cauldron, I would truly and gladly accept it!

units.zh: 魏景元中，蜀平，省東廣漢郡。
units.literal: Wei Jingyuan era Shu fell and Eastern Guanghan Commandery was abolished.
units.idiomatic: Wei annexation canceled Eastern Guanghan.

units.zh: 及武帝泰始二年，分益州置梁州，以漢中屬焉。
units.literal: Emperor Wu the second year of Taishi split Yizhou to create Liangzhou with Hanzhong attached.
units.idiomatic: the second year of Taishi lifted Liangzhou from Yizhou and parked Hanzhong inside.

units.zh: 七年，又分益州置寧州。
units.literal: Seventh year further split Yizhou to establish Ningzhou.
units.idiomatic: Year seven added Ningzhou west of Yizhou.

units.zh: 益州統郡八，縣四十四，戶十四萬九千三百。
units.literal: Yizhou oversees eight commanderies, forty-four counties, and one hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred households.
units.idiomatic: Eight commanderies, forty-four counties, one hundred forty-nine thousand three hundred households.

units.zh: 遣居河南，所謂死而生之，亡而存之，懷我德惠，終無叛逆。」
units.literal: Sending them to dwell south of the Yellow River—this is what is called giving life to the dead and preserving the perished; cherishing our virtue and kindness, they will in the end never rebel."
units.idiomatic: Settle them south of the river—give life to the doomed and restore the lost. Grateful for our kindness, they will never rebel."

units.zh: 魏征又曰：「晉代有魏時胡落，分居近郡，平吳已後，郭欽、江統勸武帝逐出塞外；
units.literal: Wei Zheng again said: "In the Jin era there were barbarian tribes from Wei times, scattered among neighboring commanderies; after Wu was pacified, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier passes;
units.idiomatic: Wei Zheng answered again: "Under Jin there were Wei-era barbarian tribes scattered through the neighboring commanderies. After Wu was pacified, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the passes;

units.zh: 不用欽等言，數年之後，遂傾瀍、洛。
units.literal: He did not heed the words of Qin and the others; within a few years, then Chan and Luo were overturned.
units.idiomatic: he ignored them, and within a few years the capitals at Chan and Luo were overturned.
